title: A Fatal Case of Massive Pulmonary Embolism: A Call to Equitable Access to Mechanical Circulatory Support and Personalized Cardiac  Arrest Management
content: We present the case of a 45-year-old woman who suffered a cardiac arrest likely due to pulmonary embolism and underwent complex resuscitation. First, we highlight the urgent need to make mechanical circulatory support equitably accessible, as current systems remain strongly dependent on geography. To address this inequity, we propose the development and evaluation of hub-and-spoke models in which mobile teams can rapidly initiate extracorporeal support at referring hospitals before transfer. Second, we explore the potential roles of advanced diagnostic, therapeutic, and monitoring adjuncts, including resuscitative transesophageal echocardiography, aortic occlusion catheters, and transcranial Doppler, in tailoring life support to the patient’s physiology.
